utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-03-66-A, the Prosecutor versus Fatmir Limaj, Haradin Bala, and Isak Musliu.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I please have the appearances of the parties. The Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MS. CAREY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Kristina Carey for the Prosecution. I'm joined today by my co-counsel, Milbert Shin, and our case manager, Kim Fischer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Carey. Counsel for Mr. Limaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: If it pleases Your Honour, Karim Khan for the respondent, Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Khan. Counsel for Mr. Bala.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good evening, Your Honour. Gregor Guy-Smith appearing on behalf of Mr. Bala who is present with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. Counsel for Mr. Musliu.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: May it please Your Honour, Steven Powles appearing on behalf of the respondent Isak Musliu.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I understand that Mr. Limaj and Mr. Musliu, who are not currently incarcerated, are not attending the Status Conference. Would their respective counsel kindly confirm this for the record? Mr. Khan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: And Mr. Powles.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. Similarly, I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Bala, however, is present today, and I want to make sure that he can follow our proceedings. Mr. Bala, can you hear the proceedings in a language you can understand? Mr. Bala? THE APPELLANT BALA: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bala. You may be seated. This is, as you know, a Status Conference called in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Rule 65 bis (B) requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days of the last Status Conference to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including the mental and physical condition of that person. The last Status Conference in this case was held on 4 May 2006. As Mr. Bala is currently detained at the UN Detention Unit, I want to start by asking him whether there are any issues he would like to raise at this time. Mr. Bala, do you have any issues that you would like to raise? Do you have any concerns regarding your mental or physical well being, Mr. Bala? THE APPELLANT BALA: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. Everything is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bala. You may be seated. Now I would like to ask counsel for Mr. Limaj and Mr. Musliu whether there are any issues that Mr. Limaj and Mr. Musliu would like to raise through counsel. Counsel for Mr. Limaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, there is not, although I will take the opportunity with your leave to thank my learned friends from the Prosecution and my learned friends for the Defence, and of course the graciousness of Your Honour, in rescheduling this matter from 8.00 a.m. to later in the evening. I am very grateful for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Khan. Now we will hear from counsel for Mr. Musliu.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm grateful. Nothing to raise on behalf of Mr. Musliu.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I am pleased to note that since our last Status Conference the parties have filed a number of briefs. The briefing of both the Prosecution's appeal and Mr. Bala's appeal is now complete. The Appeals Chamber will of course try to read through the briefs and schedule oral argument on the appeals as soon as possible. Before concluding this Status Conference, I want to ask counsel for the Prosecution and Defence whether they've any other issues that they would like to raise at this time. Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. CAREY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. The Prosecution has nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There is nothing to be raised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: No, thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we concur. I'm grateful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Before we adjourn, there is one last piece of business that I would like to take care of. In accordance with Rule 65 bis we will need to have another Status Conference on or before 27 December. Tuesday, 5 December, would, I believe, be a good day for our next Status Conference. So I would like everybody to plan on having a Status Conference that day. Later in the fall, I will hopefully send out an order confirming that the Status Conference will be held on that date. The order will also let everybody know the time of the conference and the courtroom in which it will be held. I thank the parties for their attendance and call the proceedings to a close. Thank you very much.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
